results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** The fixed Fibonacci convention, the normalized generators
$B_i=rI+(1-r)P_i$, the total-charge-$\tau$ fusion-path basis, and
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[F1] The path projectors are orthogonal, satisfy the adjacent and distant
relations, and the normalized matrices are a unitary B6 representation.
[[lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-b6-path-projectors-and-artin]]

[F2] The coefficient field $\mathbb Q(r,\sqrt\phi)$ has the stated
degree-eight presentation and admits the exact $\mathbb F_{31}$
specialization. [[lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-coefficient-ring-specialization]]

[F3] Integer powers of a circle rotation with irrational angle are dense.
[[lem-qc-irrational-rotation-dense-on-circle]]

[F4] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, closed subgroups of finite-dimensional Lie
groups are Lie subgroups and their Lie algebras are bracket closed.
[[thm-cartans-closed-subgroup-theorem]]
[[prop-the-lie-algebra-of-a-lie-subgroup-is-a-lie-subalgebra]]

[F5] $\mathfrak{su}(8)$ has real dimension $63$ and consists of the
trace-zero skew-Hermitian matrices.
[[ex-unitary-and-special-unitary-lie-groups]]

[F6] $SU(8)$ is path connected. [[lem-qc-tqc-special-unitary-connected]]

[F7] Fusion-tree dimensions are counted by summing products of the vertex
multiplicities over all admissible internal charges.
[[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]

[F8] The current Fibonacci data carrier states $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$
and fixes $R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$ and the displayed unitary $F$ block in
the stated gauge. [[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]]

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is countable choice, the exact axiom in [F4].
[[def-countable-choice]]

[A2] Assume the Fibonacci fusion rule and the fixed-chirality $F/R$ data
stated in [[lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-b6-path-projectors-and-artin]].



1.1 The fusion rule and $F/R$ convention in [F8], together with recurrence [F7], give $\dim V(\tau^3\to1)=1$, $\dim V(\tau^3\to\tau)=2$, and $\dim V(\tau^4\to\tau)=3$. The eight paths in $\mathcal P_\tau$ thus decompose by the first-three-charge label: charge $1$ contributes $1\cdot2=2$ dimensions, and charge $\tau$ contributes $V(\tau^3\to\tau)\otimes V(\tau\otimes\tau^3\to\tau)$ of dimension $2\cdot3=6$. The operator $C:=B_1B_2^{-1}$ is identity on the first summand. On the two-dimensional first-three charge-$\tau$ factor it has determinant $1$ and trace $\phi^{-2}$, so the full spectrum of $C$ is $1$ with multiplicity $2$ and $e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta}$ each with multiplicity $3$, where $2\cos\theta=\phi^{-2}$. [F1, F7, F8, A2, algebra]

2.1 The minimal polynomial of $\phi^{-2}$ is $x^2-3x+1$, whose other root is $\phi^2>2$. If $e^{i\theta}$ were a root of unity, every algebraic conjugate of its trace $e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}$ would be a sum of two roots of unity and have absolute value at most $2$, contradicting the conjugate $\phi^2$. Thus $\theta/(2\pi)$ is irrational. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F3], powers of $C$ are dense in the circle $T=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,e^{it}I_3,e^{-it}I_3)$ after choosing an eigenbasis. Let $H$ be the closure of the normalized B6 image in $U(8)$. Then $T\subseteq H$, so the nonzero tangent $X=C-C^{-1}$ lies in $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. [F3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Starting with $Z_0=X$, construct a list as follows, all over $\mathbb F_{31}$ for the independence tests: repeatedly scan $\operatorname{Ad}_i(Z_j)=B_iZ_jB_i^{-1}$ in current-list order $j$ and generator order $i=1,\ldots,5$, appending a word exactly when its specialized row is independent of previous rows. Using the resulting list as a snapshot, scan commutators $[Z_j,Z_i]$ in lexicographic order $j>i$, again appending exactly the independent rows. Repeat full rounds until none is appended. Each accepted word is an adjoint or bracket applied to earlier Lie algebra elements, so it lifts to $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. Unitary conjugation and commutators preserve traceless skew-Hermitian matrices. [F1, F4, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 [F2] makes reduction of every coefficient and denominator in these words well defined. The exact integer-arithmetic certificate `research/scaffold-audit-2026-10-16/topological-quantum-computing/b6-su8-lie-rank-certificate.py` selects 63 words by the procedure of step 4.1 (the script labels them $Y_0,\ldots,Y_{62}$; this proof renames them $Z_0,\ldots,Z_{62}$) and returns determinant $22$ for the $63\times63$ minor formed from the first $63$ row-major coordinates of these matrices. A zero algebraic determinant would map to zero in $\mathbb F_{31}$; since $22\ne0$, the exact determinant is nonzero. The omitted coordinate is the final diagonal entry, determined by trace zero. Thus the selected traceless skew-Hermitian matrices are linearly independent over $\mathbb C$. [F2, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 By [F5], $\mathfrak{su}(8)$ has real dimension $63$. Step 5.1 supplies $63$ independent elements of $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$, so $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\mathfrak{su}(8)$. Each $B_i$ has determinant $r^{8-3}=r^5$ by [F1], hence $\det(H)\subseteq\langle r^5\rangle$ is finite. The identity component therefore lies in $SU(8)$ and has full dimension; it is open there. By [F6], $SU(8)$ is connected, so the identity component equals $SU(8)$. Hence the B6 closure contains $SU(8)$. [A1, A2, F1, F4, F5, F6, step 5.1, algebra] ∎



The deterministic scan in step 4.1 constructs exactly 63 Lie words from the
same initial tangent $X=C-C^{-1}$ by conjugations and Lie brackets; the script
prints their names as $Y_0,\ldots,Y_{62}$, which this proof calls
$Z_0,\ldots,Z_{62}$. The exact $63\times63$ minor has determinant $22$
modulo $31$, so these Lie words are independent; each generator has
 determinant $r^5$. These are the projection data used by the
joint-closure argument; they do not assert an efficient braid compiler.

**Given:** The orthogonal projection $P$, the block-unitary target $T$, the
ambient unitary $G$, and $\delta\ge0$.

[F1] Logical block error and leakage are
$\|PGP-U P\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\|(I-P)GP\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ after identifying
$U$ with its zero-on-the-complement extension.
[[def-qc-tqc-logical-error-and-leakage]]

[F2] The operator norm is the maximum of $\|Tx\|$ over unit vectors $x$.
[[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]]



1.1 Since $T$ preserves both summands, $PTP=UP$ on $PV$ and $(I-P)TP=0$. Thus $PGP-UP=P(G-T)P$. For any $y\in V$, the decomposition $y=Py+(I-P)y$ is orthogonal, so the Pythagorean identity gives $\|Py\|\le\|y\|$ and $\|(I-P)y\|\le\|y\|$. Applying the first inequality to $y=(G-T)Px$ and to $x$, for every unit vector $x$, yields $\|P(G-T)Px\|\le\|(G-T)Px\|\le\|G-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Taking the maximum in [F2] proves the norm is at most $\delta$. This is the logical block error bound. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Similarly $(I-P)GP=(I-P)(G-T)P$ because $(I-P)TP=0$. Use the second contraction proved in step 1.1: for every unit $x$, $\|(I-P)(G-T)Px\|\le\|(G-T)Px\|\le\|G-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$. Taking the maximum gives the leakage bound. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** $u=\phi^{-1}$, $v=\phi^{-1/2}$,
$r=e^{-3\pi i/5}$, $F=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix}$,
$B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,r)$, and $B_2=FB_1F$.

[F1] The matrix formulas, unitarity, Artin relation, and noncommutation are
verified directly in [[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-qubit-matrices]].

[F5] A complex normal endomorphism of a finite-dimensional inner-product
space has an orthonormal eigenbasis.
[[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]

[F2] If $\alpha/(2\pi)$ is irrational, the powers of the circle rotation
$e^{i\alpha}$ are dense in the unit circle.
[[lem-qc-irrational-rotation-dense-on-circle]]

[F3] A closed subgroup of a finite-dimensional real Lie group is an embedded
Lie subgroup under ACω; its tangent space is bracket closed.
[[thm-cartans-closed-subgroup-theorem]]
[[prop-the-lie-algebra-of-a-lie-subgroup-is-a-lie-subalgebra]]

[F4] The quotient map $q:SU(2)\to PU(2)$ is a two-sheeted covering,
and $PU(2)$ is isomorphic to the connected Lie group $SO(3)$.
[[lem-qc-tqc-pu2-is-so3]]

[A1] Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, exactly the hypothesis of [F3] and [F4].
[[def-countable-choice]]



1.1 Put $C=B_1B_2^{-1}$. Using $F^2=I$, $v^2=u$, and $r+r^{-1}=-u$, direct multiplication gives $\det C=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}C=r+r^{-1}+(2-r-r^{-1})u^2=u^2$; the last equality uses $u^2+u=1$, since $(2+u)u^2=1$. Thus the eigenvalues of the unitary $C$ are $e^{i\theta}$ and $e^{-i\theta}$, with $2\cos\theta=u^2=\phi^{-2}$. [F1, F5, algebra]

2.1 The number $\phi^{-2}$ has minimal polynomial $x^2-3x+1$, whose other root is $\phi^2>2$. If $e^{i\theta}$ were a root of unity, then $e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}$ would have all algebraic conjugates of absolute value at most $2$, since every such conjugate is a sum of two roots of unity. The conjugate $\phi^2>2$ contradicts this. Hence $\theta/(2\pi)$ is irrational. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Since $2\theta/(2\pi)=\theta/\pi$ is irrational, [F2] shows that the projective powers of $C$ are dense in the circle $T=\{[\operatorname{diag}(e^{it},e^{-it})]:t\in\mathbb R\}\subset PU(2)$ after choosing an eigenbasis. This circle is contained in the closure $H$ of the projective braid image. By [A1] and [F3], $H$ is a Lie subgroup. Let $q:SU(2)\to PU(2)$ be the quotient map from [F4]. In an eigenbasis, $C-C^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(2i\sin\theta,-2i\sin\theta)$, so $dq(C-C^{-1})$ is a nonzero tangent to $T$ and belongs to $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Write $X=dq(C-C^{-1})\in\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. Conjugation by $[B_1]$ sends $T$ to a circle with tangent $\operatorname{Ad}_{[B_1]}X$. If these circles had the same axis, the rotation in $SO(3)$ induced by $[B_1]$ would either preserve or reverse that axis. A reversing rotation is a half-turn, but this projective generator has angle $3\pi/5\ne\pi$. If it preserved the oriented axis, it would commute projectively with $C$. Choose a determinant-one lift of $[B_1]$ to $SU(2)$, using [F4]. Its conjugate of $C$ would then be either $C$ or $-C$, because the kernel of $q$ is $\{\pm I\}$. The second case contradicts invariance of trace and $\operatorname{tr}C=\phi^{-2}\ne0$, so $B_1$ would commute with $C$, and hence with $B_2$, contrary to [F1]. Therefore the two axes are nonparallel. Under the standard identification of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ with $\mathbb R^3$, the Lie bracket is the cross product up to a nonzero scalar; the bracket of two nonparallel axes is nonzero and independent of both. Thus $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\mathfrak{so}(3)$ by [F3]. [A1, F1, F3, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 The identity component $H^0$ has the full dimension of connected $SO(3)$, so it is an open subgroup. A connected group has no proper open subgroup; therefore $H^0=SO(3)$ and $H=SO(3)$. By [F4], the projective braid image is dense in $PU(2)$. The only choice assumption is [A1], and the conclusion is projective; no efficient braid-length bound follows. [A1, F3, F4, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The triple code, the full fusion space, an adjacent pair of
triples, $U\in U(4)$, $\delta>0$, and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[F1] The normalized six-strand image has closure containing
$SU(5)\times SU(8)$, and for each $U\in U(4)$ there are determinant-one
extensions $T_1=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}$ and
$T_\tau=U\oplus\operatorname{diag}((\det U)^{-1},1,1,1)$.
[[lem-qc-tqc-b6-joint-su5-su8-density]]
[[def-qc-tqc-six-anyon-encoded-subspace]]

[F2] A full-space norm bound by $\delta$ bounds logical block error and
leakage by $\delta$.
[[thm-qc-tqc-block-approximation-error]]

[F3] A local braid on a tensor factor acts as its braid operator tensored with
the identity on spectator factors; unitary fusion-tree reassociation changes
basis by a unitary.
[[thm-qc-tqc-gauge-covariance]]

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is countable choice.
[[def-countable-choice]]



1.1 Each triple has fusion factor $V(\tau^3\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^2$. Associating the $n$ triple charges first gives the code factorization $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$; the second factor records all spectator fusion paths. This is an orthogonal fusion-tree decomposition by [F1, F3]. [given, F1, F3, construct]

1.2 Reassociate so the chosen adjacent six strands are first. Their total charge is $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, giving the orthogonal ambient decomposition $$V(\tau^{3n}\to c)\cong \bigoplus_{a=1,\tau}V(\tau^6\to a)\otimes V(a\otimes\tau^{3n-6}\to c).$$ The second factor contains every remaining fusion path and every multiplicity of the spectator triples. By [F3], a local six-strand braid $b$ acts as $\bigoplus_a\rho_a(b)\otimes I$ in this decomposition. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 For each $a$, let $T_a$ be the target extension in [F1] and define the global ideal unitary $\mathcal W=\bigoplus_aT_a\otimes I_{V(a\otimes\tau^{3n-6}\to c)}$, omitting zero-dimensional summands. It preserves the triple code and acts there as $U$ on the selected adjacent pair and identity on all other logical and spectator factors. Joint density [F1] gives one normalized braid $b$ with $\|\rho_a(b)-T_a\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$ for both $a=1,\tau$. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, choose]

3.1 Tensoring an operator $A$ with a spectator identity preserves its norm: expand a vector in an orthonormal spectator basis to get $\|(A\otimes I)\xi\|^2=\sum_j\|A\xi_j\|^2\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\|\xi\|^2$, with equality on a maximizing unit vector tensored with one basis vector. The norm of an orthogonal direct sum is the maximum of the block norms, because the squared norm is the sum of the squared block norms. Hence $\|\rho(b)-\mathcal W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$ on the whole ambient space. [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Apply [F2] to $\rho(b)$ and $\mathcal W$. Their compression to the code differs from the target by at most $\delta$, and $(I-P)\mathcal W P=0$, so the leakage amplitude is also at most $\delta$. The norm estimate is on the whole ambient space, so it remains valid for inputs with prior leakage. The physical categorical word has the common phase of [[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]], which is harmless only after phase matching or when reported projectively. [F1, F2, step 3.1] ∎

**Given:** The RTT Yangian of [[def-yangian-gl-n-rtt-presentation]], a $\mathfrak{gl}_N$-module $W$, its action $\rho$, and a spectral shift $a\in\mathbb C$.

[F1] [[def-yangian-gl-n-rtt-presentation]]: $R_N(x)=xI+iP_N$, and the defining relation is $R_{12}(u-v)T_1(u)T_2(v)=T_2(v)T_1(u)R_{12}(u-v)$.

[F2] [[def-yangian-evaluation-module]]: the proposed generator action is $t_{ij}(u)=\delta_{ij}I_W-i\rho(E_{ij})/(u-a)$, and the dual-natural action is $E_{ij}f^k=-\delta_{ik}f^j$.

[F3] [[def-matrix-units]]: $E_{ij}$ is the matrix with entries $(E_{ij})_{rs}=\delta_{ri}\delta_{sj}$.

[F4] [[lem-yangian-rtt-component-commutator-form]]: $x[t_{ij}(u),t_{kl}(v)]=i(t_{kj}(v)t_{il}(u)-t_{kj}(u)t_{il}(v))$ for $x=u-v$ is equivalent to the matrix RTT relation.



1.1 Let $e_1,\ldots,e_N$ be the standard column basis. By [F3], $E_{ij}e_s=\delta_{js}e_i$, so $E_{ij}E_{kl}e_s=\delta_{jk}\delta_{ls}e_i=(\delta_{jk}E_{il})e_s$ for every $s$. Hence $E_{ij}E_{kl}=\delta_{jk}E_{il}$ and $[E_{ij},E_{kl}]=\delta_{jk}E_{il}-\delta_{li}E_{kj}$. On a dual basis vector $f^s$, the explicit commutator is $[\rho^\vee(E_{ij}),\rho^\vee(E_{kl})]f^s=\delta_{ks}\delta_{il}f^j-\delta_{is}\delta_{jk}f^l$. The right side is also $\rho^\vee(\delta_{jk}E_{il}-\delta_{li}E_{kj})f^s$, by the same formula. Thus the dual-natural operators satisfy the matrix-unit bracket and form a $\mathfrak{gl}_N$-representation. [given, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Put $x=u-v$, $U=u-a$, and $V=v-a$. By [F4], the required component identity is the RTT relation to check. Under [F2], its left side is $-x(\delta_{jk}\rho(E_{il})-\delta_{li}\rho(E_{kj}))/(UV)$ by the bracket relation. In the parenthesized difference on the right, the quadratic terms cancel because both are $(-i)^2\rho(E_{kj})\rho(E_{il})/(UV)$. Its linear terms are $-i\delta_{kj}\rho(E_{il})(U^{-1}-V^{-1})-i\delta_{il}\rho(E_{kj})(V^{-1}-U^{-1})=ix(\delta_{jk}\rho(E_{il})-\delta_{li}\rho(E_{kj}))/(UV)$, since $V-U=-x$. Multiplication by the outer factor $i$ therefore gives the same left side. Thus every component RTT relation holds. [given, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The component relations are exactly the coefficients of the matrix relation [F1]. Thus the images of every defining relation vanish, so the assignment on the free generators factors through the RTT quotient and defines the representation $W(a)$. For $W=V_N^\vee$, its auxiliary matrix is $I+iP_N/(u-a)$ by the explicit sum $\sum_{i,j}E_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}=P_N$; multiplying by $u-a$ gives $R_N(u-a)$. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The finite-dimensional periodic chain, its polynomial monodromy and trace, and the monodromy RTT relation.

[F1] [[def-yangian-periodic-fundamental-chain]]: $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional, $M_0(u)$ is polynomial in $u$, and $\tau(u)=\operatorname{tr}_0M_0(u)$ is the ordinary auxiliary trace.

[F2] [[lem-yangian-periodic-monodromy-satisfies-rtt]]: $R_{00'}(u-v)M_0(u)M_{0'}(v)=M_{0'}(v)M_0(u)R_{00'}(u-v)$ for every $u,v$.

[F3] [[prop-yangian-rational-r-matrix-yang-baxter-and-invertibility]]: $R_N(d)$ has a two-sided inverse if $d\notin\{i,-i\}$.



1.1 Suppose $u-v\notin\{i,-i\}$. Multiplying the RTT identity [F2] on the right by $R_{00'}(u-v)^{-1}$, which exists by [F3], gives $R_{00'}M_0(u)M_{0'}(v)R_{00'}^{-1}=M_{0'}(v)M_0(u)$. Take the ordinary trace over the two auxiliary spaces. For a finite-dimensional auxiliary matrix $X$ with coefficients in $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$ and an invertible scalar auxiliary matrix $R$, $\operatorname{tr}(RXR^{-1})=\operatorname{tr}(X)$: writing entries, $\sum_{i,j,k}R_{ij}X_{jk}(R^{-1})_{ki}=\sum_{j,k}X_{jk}\sum_i(R^{-1})_{ki}R_{ij}=\sum_jX_{jj}$, since scalar entries commute with the coefficients and $R^{-1}R=I$. Thus the trace of the left side is $\operatorname{tr}_{00'}(M_0(u)M_{0'}(v))$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 The tensor-space trace of $M_0(u)M_{0'}(v)$ equals $\tau(u)\tau(v)$, since the two auxiliary factors are independent and the coefficient order is $u$ then $v$. The trace of $M_{0'}(v)M_0(u)$ equals $\tau(v)\tau(u)$ by the same index expansion with the coefficient order reversed. Step 1.1 therefore proves $[\tau(u),\tau(v)]=0$ whenever $u-v\notin\{i,-i\}$. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Each matrix entry of $[\tau(u),\tau(v)]$ is a polynomial in $u,v$ by [F1]. For every fixed $v$, it vanishes for all but at most two values of $u$ by step 2.1, hence is the zero polynomial in $u$; consequently it vanishes for all $u,v$. This proves the assertion also at $u-v=\pm i$, where the auxiliary $R$ is singular. [given, F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
